title: Rewrite trace hooks and parallel metric-ingest pipeline to reduce tail CPU and allocation overhead
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Production services show intermittent CPU spikes (up to +30%) and elevated p99 latency correlated with bursty tracing and metrics flushes. Root cause analysis points to: 1) tracing hook callbacks running synchronously in hot code paths and performing allocations/serialization; 2) the metrics ingestion path doing synchronous encoding and remote uploads under request critical threads; 3) opportunistic locks in the exporter path creating head-of-line blocking during high concurrency.

Goal: Reduce tail CPU and allocations for request-handling threads by moving heavy work off the hot path, rewriting tracing hook contracts to be allocation-minimal, and introducing a parallel buffered metric ingestion pipeline that batches and backpressures outside the request context. Target improvements: 20-40% reduction in CPU attributed to telemetry in busy services, 30-60% reduction in p99 request latency attributable to observability work, and a measurable drop in runtime GC pressure.

Scope: Services using the current in-process OTEL integration across the runtime and gateway layers. Work includes API contract changes for tracing hooks, an in-process background worker pool for serialization/flush, lightweight sampling/shard-aware batching, and a compatibility shim for third-party exporters. The change must be opt-in via feature flag and rolled out canary-first to low-traffic clusters before global rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Production canary shows <=10% increase in overall p50 latency and p99 latency reduced by >=15% vs baseline during burst tests
Telemetry CPU attribution in flamegraphs shows 20-40% reduction for tracing/metrics code paths on representative services
No lost spans or metrics in end-to-end verification for 99.99% of events during synthetic load tests; any transient backpressure results in documented buffered backlog and retry behavior
Feature flag exists to toggle new ingest pipeline and tracing hook behavior per service/cluster
Compatibility shim maintains existing exporter contracts for the top 3 outbound destinations (vendor-a, vendor-b, internal-collector)
implementation_plan: Prototype: implement zero-alloc tracing hook interface and local background serialize worker in a fork branch (ENG-161235)

Bench: microbench hot-path allocations and CPU with representative workloads and compare with baseline
(bench artifacts uploaded to PR)

Parallel pipeline: introduce buffered ring-queue + worker pool for metric encoding and remote flush with per-shard backpressure
(ENG-161236)
Compatibility: add exporter shim that converts new wire format to existing exporter expectations; add opt-in feature flag
Canary rollout: enable flag for small subset of clusters, monitor logs/dropped-events, CPU, and tail latency dashboards
Iterate: address feedback in canary, expand rollout, remove legacy hot-path code once stable
risks: Behavioral change for consumers of tracing hook callbacks — some internal libraries invoked side-effectful logic; mitigation: clear contract doc and deprecation window
Backpressure could cause increased memory transiently during bursts if workers can't keep up; mitigation: adaptive shard-sizes and a bounded retry queue with metrics and alerting
Exporter incompatibility with a small number of legacy partners; mitigation: compatibility shim and partner coordination during rollout
metrics_to_track: CPU% attributed to observability (flamegraphs / pprof tags)
p99 request latency before/after feature flag
span and metric delivery success rate (per-minute)
background queue length and worker lateness metrics
rollout_notes: Gate behind feature flag: observability.ingest.v2 = false by default
Start with gateway staging cluster for 24h smoke, then org-internal canary (5% traffic) for 72h
Escalation: automatic rollback if span/metric delivery falls below 99.9% for 1h or CPU increase >20% sustained
Communicate breaking contract changes to internal SDK teams and include migration guide and tests
qa_plan: Unit tests for new tracing hook surface and exporter shim
Integration tests that run full end-to-end ingest with synthetic spans/metrics and assert no loss under transient load
Load tests reproducing bursty behavior from production traces using recorded trace-replay harness
Chaos test: kill worker processes and verify bounded backpressure and retry semantics
notes: Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8712 (initial zero-alloc hook + bench) — awaiting code review
Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/observability/ingest-proto?orgId=1 shows 28% alloc/s reduction for service-x in synthetic run
Follow-up: schedule 1:1 with SDK owners to review the tracing hook contract and migration timeline
Related: aligns with runtime-1.30 perf goals and reduces chargeable token overhead from telemetry in hosted API
